title: Purification and preservation of satellite cells from human skeletal muscle
protocol: Handle the muscle biopsy under sterile conditions.
Immerse the muscle biopsy in cold collection media immediately after removal.
Place the muscle biopsy in a 50 mL conical tube filled with 25 mL of cold muscle collection media.
Keep the conical tube containing the muscle biopsy on ice at all times.
Weigh the muscle sample by taring an empty 50 mL conical tube and placing the sample inside carefully using sterile forceps.
Record the weight for future calculations.
Note the type of muscle, age of the individual, and gender.
Document additional information such as history of diseases and medications taken if relevant.
Remove connective and adipose tissue from the muscle sample.
Remove cauterized or devitalized tissue contaminants from the muscle sample.
Remove any surgical foreign bodies from the muscle sample.
Reserve a fraction of the muscle sample for other experiments as needed.
Work efficiently to aid cell viability after sorting.
Maintain sterility throughout the entire process using a biological safety laminar flow cabinet/cell culture cabinet class II or III.
Immerse muscle tissue in prewarmed digestion media during mechanical dissociation.
Minimize shear stress on cells by avoiding mashing, grinding of tissue, and rapid pipetting.
Prewarm the digestion media with collagenase at 37°C.
Prewarm trypsin at 37°C.
Label all dissection equipment clearly if processing multiple biological samples simultaneously to avoid contamination.
Dispose of used equipment appropriately after bleaching with 10% bleach solution and placing in a biohazard trash bin.
Use a box cutting blade and size 15 disposable scalpel for tissue mincing within a 10 cm glass Petri dish.
Mince muscle tissue in a small amount (approximately 3 mL) of digestion media to enhance mechanical digestion.
Cut the muscle tissue into pieces smaller than 1 mm² using the box cutting blade and scalpel, avoiding crushing or smashing the tissue.
Transfer thoroughly minced muscle to a 50 mL conical tube.
Use sterile PBS to retrieve muscle pieces from the Petri dish and place them in the conical tube.
Resuspend minced muscle in prewarmed digestion media containing collagenase at a ratio of 10 mL of media per gram of muscle.
For a 5 g muscle sample, use 50 mL of digestion media divided into two conical tubes each with 25 mL of media and muscle.
Place the tubes on a mixing platform inside a 37°C incubator for 35 minutes, shaking gently and continuously.
Every 10 minutes during the incubation period, swirl and flick the tubes to dislodge the pellet and ensure enzyme penetration into myofibers.
Wash 13 gauge needle well in 70% ethanol.
Rinse 13 gauge needle with milli Q water.
Rinse 13 gauge needle with sterile PBS.
Aspirate sterile PBS through syringe attached to needle a few times.
Pass tissue suspension through 13 gauge needle attached to 60 mL syringe about 10-20 times until tissue is grossly dissociated.
Pass the suspension through a 16-gauge needle attached to a 20 mL syringe about 10–20 times.
Pass the suspension through a 19-gauge needle about 10 times.
Slowly move media with tissue up and down the syringe.
If clogs occur, gently pull them out of the eye of the needle with tweezers.
Remove connective tissue from media if present.
Mince muscle clumps on Petri dish more with box cutting blade, then pass through needle 10 times more.
Stop passing suspension through needles once solution is homogeneous and no longer clogs the needle.
Avoid generating bubbles during passage; do not aspirate air.
Proceed gently to avoid spilling precious sample.
Place the sample back in the 37°C mixing incubator for another 35 min.
Resuspend the pellet by aspirating with a wide-bore 1 mL tip several times during this stage of the incubation.
Warm 3 mL of 0.25% trypsin for every gram of tissue to 37°C for later use.
Prepare DNase media fresh and keep it at room temperature.
After 1 hour and 10 minutes total time of tissue digestion, dilute and rinse the suspension with ice cold PBS without Ca++ or Mg+ by filling up the 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the sample at 2,000 rpm (500 RCF) for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet completely in residual supernatant and wash again with ice cold PBS without Ca++ or Mg+.
Pipette slowly and with wide-bore pipette tips to increase cell viability.
Centrifuge the sample again at 2,000 rpm (500 RCF) for 5 min at 4°C.
Carefully aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet completely in the residual liquid.
Add 3 mL of 0.25% trypsin for every gram of tissue, mix gently.
Place the sample in a 37°C warmer for 5–12 minutes according to weight.
If less than 1 g, incubate for 5 minutes; if equal or more than 2 g, incubate for 10 minutes with a maximum of 12 minutes.
Add 1.5 mL of FBS per gram of tissue to quench the trypsin and mix gently by swirling the tube.
Fill up to the top with 2% FBS in sterile PBS.
Centrifuge the sample at 2,000 rpm (500 RCF) for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant after centrifugation at 2,000 rpm (500 RCF) for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Take utmost care to avoid touching the pellet when aspirating the supernatant and leave enough supernatant.
Incubate the sample with DNase media at a final concentration of 10 μg/mL in DMEM.
Add 3–5 mL of DNase to the conical tube containing the sample and incubate for 5 to 10 minutes at room temperature.
Centrifuge the sample at 2,000 rpm (500 RCF) for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 5 mL of 2% FBS in PBS.
Place a 40 μm sterile cell strainer in a new 50 mL conical tube and label accordingly.
Pipette the cell suspension through the cell strainer using a 1 mL wide-bore tip.
Wash and recover most of the cells from the 50 mL conical tube with 2% FBS in PBS and place over the filter.
If the filter clogs, carefully centrifuge the sample for 1 minute and then filter again through a new sterile cell strainer.
Filter the sample through a cell strainer 40 μm filter fitted in a 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the filtered sample at 2,000 rpm (500 RCF) for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant, leaving 0.5 mL to protect the integrity of the pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in ice cold ACK buffer at a ratio of 1 mL per gram of tissue.
Incubate the resuspended pellet on ice for 5–7 minutes.
Wash the sample by filling the conical tube with 2% FBS in PBS.
Centrifuge the sample at 2,000 rpm (500 RCF) for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Wash the 50 mL conical tube with ice cold MACS buffer up to the top.
Centrifuge again.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 2 mL of MACS buffer.
Add 5 μL Fc blocking reagent for every gram of tissue to the conical sample tube.
Mix gently and incubate for 5 minutes on ice.
Add 5 μL of anti-CD45 magnetic beads and 2 μL of anti-CD31 magnetic beads for every gram of tissue to the sample tube.
Mix gently and incubate for 30 minutes on ice.
Set up the magnetic columns by attaching them to the MidiMACS separator magnet on a MACS MultiStand.
Add 5 mL of MACs buffer to each column and discard the first flow.
Wash the sample by filling the 50 mL conical tube with MACs buffer.
Centrifuge the sample at 2,000 rpm (500 RCF) for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant from the sample after centrifugation.
Resuspend the pellet completely in residual liquid of about 500 μL and use a wide-bore pipette to release the drop of cells on top of a MACS LD column.
Repeat washing with 2 or 3 times using 500 μL of MACS buffer.
Fill the column with 3–5 mL of MACS buffer.
Allow the sample to run through the column completely, which may take up to 45 min.
Proceed directly to incubation with FACS antibodies if the sample is equal or less than 1 g.
Incubate cells with selected panel of antibodies for 20–30 min on ice.
Prepare controls for proper calibration and gating.
Make single-color isotype compensation controls for each fluorochrome using beads.
Add 1–2 drops of beads with the same amount of 1× antibody used for that specific wavelength.
Shake the beads vigorously as they tend to clump together.
Take an aliquot from the BOUND and do not add any antibody, including cell viability marker.
Wash the samples with MACS buffer by filling the conical tube to 15 mL.
Centrifuge the samples at 2,000 rpm (500 RCF) for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the pellets gently in 100 μL MACS buffer.
Add the antibodies prepared according to panel A or B and incubate 30 min on ice, in the dark.
Add 2 mL MACS buffer to the 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the samples at 2,000 rpm (500 RCF) for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend in 200 μL or 400 μL of MACS buffer with Sytox Blue at a dilution of 1:1,000.
Centrifuge the samples at 2,000 rpm (500 RCF) for 60 seconds at 4°C.
Keep samples at 4 degrees and sort as soon as possible.
Add Sytox Blue again if the sort takes more than 1 hour.
Sort the cells into low retention 1.5 ml Eppendorf tubes to reduce the number of Hu-MuSC lost by tube wall attachment.
Ensure proper compensation, controls, and sort one sample of 1-2 g within approximately 2 hours for proper compensation.
Set up the sorter professionally before use.
Run single-color isotype compensation controls on the flow cytometer to determine gating.
Select Create Compensation under Experiments in FACS DIVA software.
Adjust the voltages and do not record yet.
Run a single compensation control for each channel.
Set the P2 on the shoulders of the positive signal per channel.
Notice where positive is.
Run compensation.
Wait for confirmation feedback that it is done.

Define the bandwidth of positive signal, tracing vertical lines over the narrow shoulders of the positive peak curve to define the range of positive fluorescence intensity for that channel and avoid or compensate for wavelength overlap with other channels.
Run the unstained control after completing compensation satisfactorily.
Record the unstained control.
Run and record the FMO control.
Run the first sample at low speed and adjust the gates.
Do not change any parameter or gating after all is compensated.
Keep these same parameters for all samples.
Ensure professional setup and calibration of the sorter.
Select 4 purity mode in the sorter window.
Check the window where the sort is saved continuously for later quality control.
Monitor the flow rate to maintain it between 1 or 2, ensuring a uniform and regular flow not exceeding 7,000 events/s for the 100 μm nozzle.
Carefully monitor parameters in the droplet camera during sorting.
Place the angle of the flow of sorted cells into the collection tubes right at the center of the tube on the collection media.
Ensure an expert support team is available to troubleshoot problems with the sorters during sorting.
Do not vortex the cells at any point as this negatively affects cell viability.
Run samples on the flow cytometer.
Sort satellite cells using the following scheme: FSC/SSC -> viable singlets -> negative depletion of CD31/CD34/CD45/sytox positive cells -> CXCR4+ -> CD56/ CD29 gate.
Collect CD31-/CD34-/CD45-/sytox-/ CXCR4+/ CD56+/ CD29+ cells directly into the satellite cell collection media tubes.
Record flow rate and drop 1 during sorting.
Note the number of sorted cells and the percentage of the sorted population over the overall cell population.
Keep vials on ice after sorting and proceed immediately with experiments or cell cryopreservation.
Export and save all FCS files for quality control and sort record.
Retrospective analysis of the sample is recommended after sorting using Flow Jo and the exported FCS files.
Centrifuge the samples for 10 minutes at 2,000 rpm (500 RCF) at 4°C to collect all cells.
Aspirate the supernatant from the centrifuged samples.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL of fresh media or 0.04% BSA in PBS for immediate use.
Prepare freezing media for cryopreservation if needed.
Count and assess cell viability using Countess and Trypan Blue staining after sorting.
Use Countess and Trypan Blue staining to assess cell numbers and viability, ensuring a minimum of 10,000 cells for accurate quantification.
Plate cells on Matrigel-precoated dishes.
Seed cells for at least 4 hours at 37°C.
Fix cells with PFA 4%.
Block cells.
Incubate cells with PAX7 antibody (dilution 1:50 from concentrated PAX7 antibody from DHSB).
Visualize under 20× to 40× light and fluorescence microscopy.
Isolate RNA from sorted cells using the Qiagen RNeasy kit protocol, eluting in a final volume of 14 μL.
Use RNase-free DNase during RNA isolation.
Perform cDNA transcription immediately after RNA isolation.
Amplify cDNA up to 18 cycles for PAX7 mRNA expression analysis.
Run control samples (pre-amp and no pre-amp) to verify ΔCt maintenance upon amplification.
Proceed to reverse transcription using PAX7 Taq or Sybergreen primers to detect and quantify PAX7 transcript.
Centrifuge sorted Hu-MuSC for 10 min at 2,000 rpm (500 RCF) at 4°C.
Resuspend cells in 50 μL of BSA 0.04% in PBS.
Submit the resuspended cells immediately for scRNA seq.
Centrifuge Hu-MuSC at 2,000 rpm (500 RCF) for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Wash the cells in sterile cold PBS.
Centrifuge the cells again at 2,000 rpm (500 RCF) for 4 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL of freezing media (DMEM/F12 with 20% FBS, 1× ITS, 1× glutamine, 1× gentamicin, and 10% DMSO).
Label the tube with name of the cells and sample identifiers.
Record the number of cells, the date, and any other pertinent information for your experiments.
Place the labeled tubes in an RT freezing block in a -80°C freezer.
For long term storage transfer to a liquid nitrogen cell bank and place in well labeled plastic boxes with appropriate holes to allow drainage.
Record storage details in a database.
Remove cryovial(s) from liquid or vapor-phase nitrogen storage and immediately thaw in the heating rocks or water bath at 37°C.
Transfer thawed cells gently to a 50 mL conical tube using a wide-bore pipette tip.
Rinse the cryovial with 1 mL warm complete growth medium using a wide-bore pipette tip.
Add the rinse medium dropwise (1 drop per 5 s) to the 50 mL conical tube while gently shaking the tube.
Serially dilute cells with complete growth medium by adding 2 mL of medium into an existing 2 mL cell suspension, gently swirl for 5 seconds, and leave for one minute.
Repeat serial dilution three more times to achieve a final volume of approximately 32 mL.
Centrifuge cells at 2,000 rpm (500 RCF) for 10 minutes.
Resuspend the centrifuged cells in desired medium.
